skill.name: technical-blog-writing
skill.description: Helps create developer-focused technical blog posts with clear structure, runnable examples, diagrams, distribution guidance, and reader-centered technical depth.
skill.summary: Guide technical blog drafts from idea to publishable developer article.
skill.author: inference-sh-9

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are false positives from Markdown templates and article examples. The remote installer that pipes curl output into sh is confirmed critical, and several examples invoke external services or publishing tools. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell command with manual download steps, package-manager installation, and checksum verification before execution.

remediation.issue: Examples invoke external services through infsh app run.
remediation.suggestion: State that users must approve each external command and must not send secrets, private code, or unpublished data to external apps.

remediation.issue: The distribution example can publish content to X.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before any social posting command runs, and keep publish commands separate from drafting guidance.

remediation.issue: Related-skill commands install additional community skills.
remediation.suggestion: Move npx skills add commands to optional documentation and tell users to review each skill before installation.

content.value_statement: Developer posts often lose readers through vague claims, broken examples, or weak structure. This skill gives article patterns, code guidance, visual ideas, and distribution steps for technical audiences.
actual_capabilities: Suggests structures for tutorials, explainers, postmortems, benchmarks, and architecture posts.
Provides developer-focused tone rules and common phrases to avoid.
Defines standards for runnable code examples, version pins, and error handling.
Recommends diagram types for architecture, flows, data models, and comparisons.
Outlines distribution options for blogs, developer platforms, and social channels.
Provides rough word-count ranges by technical article type.
limitations: Does not verify that code examples compile or run.
Does not replace expert review for security, performance, or incident accuracy.
Uses examples that may require external services or account access.
Does not publish content unless a separate tool or user action does it.

use_cases.title: Plan an Engineering Tutorial
use_cases.description: Turn a feature idea into a step-by-step article outline with prerequisites, runnable examples, and next steps.

use_cases.title: Write an Architecture Deep Dive
use_cases.description: Explain system choices, diagrams, trade-offs, and results for an engineering audience.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Benchmark Post
use_cases.description: Structure methodology, results, analysis, caveats, and reproducibility notes for a tool comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Blog Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the technical-blog-writing skill to create an outline for a tutorial about [topic]. Include audience level, prerequisites, sections, and a TL;DR.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Developer Tutorial
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a step-by-step tutorial for [task]. Include runnable code blocks, expected output, version notes, and common errors.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Technical Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my draft for developer clarity. Flag weak claims, missing trade-offs, broken structure, and places that need code or diagrams.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Launch Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to turn [article topic] into a publishable package. Include article structure, visual plan, SEO title options, and platform-specific distribution notes.

output_examples.input: A team wants to explain why they moved API caching to the edge.
output_examples.output: A structured architecture post with a TL;DR, problem context, request-flow diagram idea, trade-off section, measured latency results, and further reading.

output_examples.input: A developer advocate needs a beginner tutorial for building a REST API.
output_examples.output: A tutorial outline with prerequisites, setup steps, implementation milestones, expected outputs, troubleshooting notes, and a link placeholder for complete source.

output_examples.input: A technical writer has a benchmark draft with weak methodology.

best_practices: State the target reader and assumed knowledge near the start.
Test every code example and include exact dependency versions.
Include trade-offs, limitations, and sources for performance claims.
anti_patterns: Opening with generic industry context before the technical point.
Using marketing claims without benchmarks, sources, or caveats.
Publishing diagrams or snippets that readers cannot reproduce.

faq.question: What types of posts does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports tutorials, deep dives, incident reports, benchmarks, architecture posts, and distribution planning.

faq.question: Can it write complete articles?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help draft complete posts, but human review should verify code, data, and claims.

faq.question: Does it generate diagrams?
faq.answer: It suggests diagram types and example visual workflows. External tools may be needed to render final images.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with private code?
faq.answer: Avoid sharing secrets or proprietary code with external tools. Review any command before running it.

faq.question: Can it publish posts for me?
faq.answer: It includes distribution guidance. Publishing should require explicit user approval and the proper account access.

faq.question: How should I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Ask for an outline, draft, revision, or launch plan, then provide topic details and audience level.
